description: CUDA reference dump for VK-vs-CUDA first-loss parity

parity_config.note: Forces single-level GLOBAL sort (sort_mode=0). Uses new_aabb=true (CUDA C++ default + VK production path). Overrides aaa.json sort_mode=3. filter_3D passed through if PLY had it.

view_matrix.npy.convention: row-major numpy storage of cam.world_view_transform (the exact tensor CUDA receives). Because numpy row-major storage of a matrix X is byte-identical to column-major storage of X.T, and this tensor IS W2C.T, the file is byte-identical to 'column-major W2C' — which is what VK's loadCameraJson writes into Camera.view_matrix[16]. Use np.load(...).reshape(-1) for VK vec4x4 comparison.

view_matrix_cuda_native.npy.convention: Same bytes as view_matrix.npy; alias for clarity.

view_matrix_canonical_row_major.npy.convention: Mathematical W2C with standard [row, col] indexing (row-major). Transpose of view_matrix.npy viewed as a mathematical matrix. Use this if an assertion wants W2C @ p_world to give p_view directly.

proj_matrix.npy.convention: row-major numpy storage of cam.full_proj_transform (=world_view_transform @ projection_matrix, each pre-transposed). Byte-identical to 'column-major viewproj = proj * view' — matches VK Camera.viewproj_matrix.

outputs.raw_params.npz: raw_positions(N,3), raw_scales(N,3), raw_rotations(N,4) quat (r,x,y,z), raw_opacities(N,), raw_sh_coeffs(N,16,3) [gaussian, coeff, channel] (CUDA native; note VK ply_loader uses channel-major-rest so a transpose is needed on VK side).
outputs.means2D.npy: (N,2) pixel coordinates, center of image = (W/2, H/2)
outputs.rgb_colors.npy: (N,3) SH-evaluated RGB before clamp-min in kernel
outputs.sorted_ids_per_tile.npy: (R,) int32 flattened Gaussian IDs in render order, concatenated per tile.
outputs.tile_offsets.npy: (num_tiles+1,) int32 start offsets; tile i's IDs are sorted_ids_per_tile[offsets[i]:offsets[i+1]]. Last entry = R.
outputs.l1_loss.npy: (1,) float32 L1(render - gt).mean() over all CHW pixels

sort_layout_sanity.note: For sort_mode=0 (GLOBAL), stopthepop uses contiguous per-tile ranges. Contiguity checked above. If False, tile_offsets still accurately indexes each tile's segment but gaps between tiles are possible.
